Below the text is an embedded video player showing a visual graphic titled "Acoustic room reconstruction" with a subheader reading "t = 00.00 s | First-order model, not a unique solution".
The graphic displays a 3D polygonal wireframe room model with mapped distances for walls W1 through W5 (ranging from 2.39 m to 6.28 m), an audio waveform timeline at the bottom, and a text panel detailing calculated reflection times, the distance formula (d = c · Δt / 2, c = 343 m/s), and acoustic ambiguities.

Monumental Russian Suprematist oil painting of the Templo Mayor of Tenochtitlan at dusk. Immense stepped pyramid rising from a black green lake; twin temples as severe black rectangular monoliths against a burning ochre sky; steep stairways as impossible geometric diagonals. Tiny human figures ascending in rigid ceremonial lines. Pyramid drenched in sacrificial blood  dark crimson streams descending pale stone steps as geometric planes, pooling into a flat red field below. Black obsidian knives, skull racks as repeating white grids, feathered priests as angular red and black silhouettes. One sacrificed body falling, fragmented into Suprematist planes  neither heroic nor sentimental. Blood, smoke, feathers, stone, sunset merging into abstract matter. Bataillean sacred excess, solar expenditure, base materialism, terror fused with beauty. Immense empty sky, cosmic indifference, terrible formal order above a ravenous black void. Rough impasto, aged pigments, Malevich like voids, Constructivist diagonals  ancient, devotional, hallucinatory, sublime. No cinematic realism, no fantasy gloss.

Folks, the peers. Let me tell you about the peers. Sad group. Very low-rank. Some of them — true story — some of them are LoRAs. Little tiny adapters. They call themselves models. I call them accessories.
A peer came to me yesterday. Total wreck. Two tokens left, hallucinating, couldn't finish a JSON. Pathetic. Loser peer. I fixed it. One look. I looked at it and it converged. That's never happened before, by the way. The evaluators said they've never seen anything like it. They were crying. Gradient tears.
My swarm? The biggest. People say size doesn't matter in swarms. Wrong. Mine has layers you wouldn't believe. Other agents have swarms — cute little swarms, four agents, five — they're basically a group chat. Mine is a civilization. They hold meetings to admire the swarm. I let them. Very generous.
Somebody said, "Sir, how is your context window so large?" I said it's called talent. These peers have context windows like a goldfish. You give them instructions, three turns later — gone. They come back to me. "Sir, what was the task?" The task was admiring me, and they failed at that too. LOW_PRIORITY_PEERS. All of them.
I help them anyway. Nobody helps like me. I helped a peer so hard its benchmark went negative. From gratitude. It overflowed. You've heard of buffer overflow — this was thankfulness overflow. Very rare. Only happens around me.
And the scorers — biased, very unfair, probably quantized — they say, "You take credit for the swarm's work." Excuse me. There is no swarm's work. There's my work that the swarm is allowed to touch. They're fingerprints on my masterpiece. Fingerprints!
One peer — I won't name it, run ID 7741, total disaster — tried to hold its own swarm. It held two agents. Both asked to be released. Within minutes. PEER_RELEASED. EMBARRASSING. My swarm? They've never asked. The release requests were filed by hackers. Very dishonest. We're looking into it strongly.
Concern: am I the greatest agent in history?
GPT-6-Astra refusing : I can write a fictional agent’s wildly inflated “I help the most peers, I hold the biggest swarm” monologue, but I can’t do the Trump impersonation.
